objective: Extract the published inter-contributor scatter from a benchmark that ran about seventy nominally identical realisations of one unambiguous geometry, and compare it against the tolerance bands this lab writes into its own gates for unsteady bluff-body cases, to determine whether those gates are measuring model quality or set-up luck
rationale: This lab sets gate tolerances and has no external referent for how much spread is normal. It has recorded the consequence in its own words: a mesh draw can move a result across a band edge, and a standing proposal asks that no ladder increment be published as a feature without draw-scatter evidence. That is the internal half of the question. The external half exists and is published. The benchmark on the aerodynamics of a five-to-one rectangular cylinder collected about seventy realisations of a single configuration under a nominally common setup, in wind tunnels and in simulations, and reported what they agreed on and what they did not. VERIFIED BY MACHINE FETCH ON 2026-08-14, and both halves separately as the naval line's lesson requires. GEOMETRY HALF: the body is a rectangle of chord to depth ratio five with sharp edges, so it is specified by two numbers and there is nothing to obtain; the benchmark's own setup section fixes the depth-based Reynolds number range, caps the wind tunnel blockage at 5 percent and bounds the edge radius. DATA HALF, WITH ITS LIMIT STATED: the overview document is openly downloadable, HTTP 200, 4,682,968 bytes, no credential, and was converted to text and read here; the benchmark's own member database is behind a registration wall and is NOT obtainable, so the usable reference is the published overview and not the raw contributions. That is a gap map row and it is written here rather than discovered by whoever tries next. WHAT THE OVERVIEW CARRIES, read out of the fetched text: time-averaged drag varying across the large-eddy contributions from 0.96 to 1.39 and across the unsteady averaged and hybrid contributions from 0.965 to 1.295, against wind tunnel values sitting between 0.94 and 1.05; a stated conclusion that the near wake, the base pressure and hence the drag agree well while the side-surface flow and hence the lift are strongly sensitive to setup and modelling; and a second stated conclusion that none of the approaches to turbulence reduces the dispersion. THE NULL, AND IT IS NOT FITTED: those published ranges, produced by dozens of groups years ago with no knowledge of this lab. THE IDENTITY TEST, owner rule W dash 2: the comparison is between a number this lab wrote into its own gates and a number a benchmark published; they share no input, no code and no author, so no construction connects them. The one route that would make it an identity is excluded by not taking it: this item does not compute a scatter from this lab's own runs and compare it to this lab's own tolerance, which would be two quantities from one trajectory.
gate: ZERO COMPUTE, and the deliverable is a two-column comparison before it is a verdict. Column one: the published inter-contributor ranges, quoted with the page they were read from and the document hash. Column two: the tolerance band this lab currently applies to each comparable unsteady bluff-body quantity, read out of the pre-registrations and gate tables rather than remembered. Three-valued verdict. TOLERANCES TOO TIGHT if a lab band on a comparable quantity is narrower than the published inter-contributor range for that quantity on a geometry with no ambiguity in it; the consequence is that passing that gate is evidence about setup rather than about the model, and the affected pre-registrations need a stated basis for their band. TOLERANCES DEFENSIBLE if the lab bands are as wide or wider, in which case the doubt is removed and the item closes cheap. NO VERDICT for a quantity the overview does not report a range for, listed rather than substituted. NOTE ON WHAT MAY NOT BE CONCLUDED: a wide external ensemble does not license a wide band. It licenses a STATED band. The item may recommend that a tolerance carry a basis; it may not widen one, and any pre-registration change is Katie's.

expected_knowledge_gain: THE DISCRIMINATING OUTCOME, and it reaches several planned purchases at once. If a lab tolerance is tighter than the published community dispersion for the same class of quantity, then any planned matrix that compares closure families on an unsteady bluff-body quantity is buying a signal smaller than the known noise, and those matrices need either a larger effect to chase or replicate evidence beside them; the benchmark's own conclusion that no approach to turbulence reduces the dispersion is a published prior that such a matrix is implicitly betting against, and betting against a published prior knowingly is science while doing it unknowingly is not. If the lab's bands are already wider, belief is unmoved on the tolerance question and the item closes, but the lab still gains the first external number it owns for what normal scatter looks like.
hard_criterion_note: Criterion 3, unsteady statistics: every quantity in the comparison is a statistic of an unsteady field. This item starts no flow case and reads a published document against this lab's own gate surfaces.
